speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the appearance and duration of the rectal bleeding, and have you noticed any unintended weight loss or changes in bowel habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; could you tell me if you have noticed any changes in your stool caliber, such as it becoming thinner than usual, or any abdominal pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) to check for anemia.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC: Normal range, Hemoglobin: Within normal limits, Platelets: Within normal limits

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rectal bleeding daily with bowel movements. I also have No pain with defecation. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that previous assessment. While TB is a differential, I need to confirm if you have had any recent travel to endemic areas or loss of appetite. Also, have you noticed any blood clots in your stool, and does the bleeding occur before or after you pass a bowel movement? REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy with biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Varices secondary to Portal Hypertension (Cirrhosis).

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound to assess liver morphology and portal vein flow.
